title: Probing quantum chaos near a wormhole throat with a circular string
authors: Ai-chen Li, Xin-Fei Li, Xuanting Ji
abstract: We investigate whether quantum fluctuations of a circular probe string develop a quantum-chaotic response while traversing a wormhole throat. The classical circular-string embedding is periodic and radially stable, but its two physical transverse polarizations experience time-dependent tidal potentials. Expanding the world-sheet action to quadratic order, we canonically quantize these modes and construct out-of-time-ordered correlator(OTOC) amplitudes from their unequal-time commutators. For the Ellis--Bronnikov wormhole, both polarizations exhibit finite intervals of approximately exponential OTOC growth associated with the first throat passage. The corresponding dimensionless rate measured with respect to physical time is positive over the parameter range studied and generally decreases as the probe energy is increased relative to the throat scale. In the global-monopole extension, increasing the solid-angle deficit narrows the band of locally amplifiable modes and suppresses the extracted rates; a sufficiently strong defect can nearly quench the radial signal, while the angular channel retains a polarization-dependent non-monotonic structure when the energy-to-throat-scale ratio is small. These quantities characterize finite-time dynamical sensitivity in the Gaussian fluctuation sector and should not be identified with asymptotic many-body chaos or a thermodynamic phase transition. Although the numerical analysis uses two representative wormhole geometries, the construction depends only on covariant world-sheet fluctuations and real-time commutators. It therefore provides a transferable, non-holographic framework for applying quantum-chaos diagnostics directly to quantum probes in curved spacetimes.
summary: This paper examines quantum chaos near traversable wormhole throats by analyzing the OTOC growth of quantum fluctuations of a probe string. Using a quadratic approximation of the world-sheet action, the authors find evidence of finite-time exponential growth in the OTOCs for both polarizations. This work establishes a transferable, non-holographic diagnostic tool for probing quantum dynamics in regular, curved spacetimes.
main_problem: The study investigates whether quantum fluctuations of a circular probe string develop a quantum-chaotic response while traversing a wormhole throat, even when the classical radial motion is stable.
main_result: Both the Ellis–Bronnikov and global-monopole wormholes show finite intervals of exponential Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlator (OTOC) growth associated with the first throat passage. This indicates local dynamical sensitivity distinct from asymptotic chaos.
method: The authors canonically quantize the transverse fluctuation modes by expanding the world-sheet action to quadratic order and constructing OTOC amplitudes from unequal-time commutators.
model_or_system: The system involves a circular probe string embedded in curved spacetimes, specifically analyzing the Ellis–Bronnikov and global-monopole wormhole geometries. The analysis uses the Polyakov action and focuses on the quadratic fluctuations around a stable classical trajectory.
key_observables: Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlator (OTOC) amplitudes and the corresponding dimensionless rate of exponential growth.
important_parameters: Probe energy relative to the throat scale, and the solid-angle deficit ($\Delta$) in the global-monopole extension.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the quadratic approximation of the world-sheet action and the circular background ansatz, meaning the results characterize the Gaussian fluctuation sector.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the effective frequency profiles distinguishing polarizations, showing finite intervals of exponential OTOC growth at the throat, and summarizing the dependence of the dimensionless physical-time rates on the solid-angle deficit.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem by contrasting the regular classical motion with the potential for quantum chaos. It details the mathematical framework by quantizing the transverse fluctuations via the quadratic action, calculates the OTOCs, and presents results for specific wormhole models, concluding with a discussion of the physical interpretation and limitations.
why_interesting: The methodology—applying OTOC diagnostics to a regular, horizonless geometry—provides a non-holographic, transferable framework for studying quantum chaos in curved spacetimes, which is highly relevant for theoretical work on quantum gravity and spacetime dynamics.
